question.text: At <math><mn>143</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mo>,</mo></math> the reaction of <math><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></math> with <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> produces a xenon compound <math><mi mathvariant="normal">Y</mi><mo>.</mo></math> The total number of lone pair(s) of electrons present on the whole molecule of <math><mi mathvariant="normal">Y</mi></math> is __________

solution.text:
XeF4 + O2F2 → XeF6 + O2

So Y is XeF6

Each F atom contains three lone pairs and Xe atom contain one lone pair.

so total lone pair=3×6+1=19

Total L.P=19.
